DILG DAGO-NG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. 5'. APR 23 2025 KARL SHANE PIORNATO Rheoshane214@gmail.com Dear Mr. Piornato. This has reference to your email communication dated 26 March 2025 seeking clarification on the legality of the LGU Buenavista Municipal Budget Office's directive to remove a Barangay Administrator on the ground that only persons with a law degree or graduate of courses related to public administration may hold the position. We respond. At the outset, the Local Government Code (LGC), particularly, Sections 4431, 4542 and 4633, only mentions the appointment of an Administrator in the provincial, city and municipal levels. The LGC provides for neither the position of Administrator nor its qualifications in the Barangay level. However, Section 387 of the LGC allows the Sangguniang Barangay to create such other positions or offices as may be deemed necessary to carry out the purposes of the barangay government.4 1 Section 443. Officials of the Municipal Government. — xxx (b) In addition thereto, the mayor may appoint a municipal administrator, a municipal legal officer, a municipal agriculturist a municipal environment and natural resources officer, a municipal social welfare and development officer, a municipal architect, and a municipal information officer. 2 Section 454. Officials of the City Government. (a) There shall be in each city a mayor, a vice-mayor, sangguniang panlungsod members, a secretary to the sangguniang panlungsod, a city treasurer, a city assessor, a city accountant, a city budget officer, a city planning and development coordinator, a city engineer, a city health officer, a city civil registrar, a city administrator, a city legal officer, a city veterinarian, a city social welfare and development officer, and a city general services officer 3 Section 463. Officials of the Provincial Govemment. (a) There shall be in each province a governor, a vice-governor, members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, a secretary to the sangguniang panlalawigan, a provincial treasurer, a provincial assessor, a provincial accountant, a provincial engineer, a provincial budget officer, a provincial planning and development coordinator, a provincial legal officer, a provincial administrator, a provincial health officer, a provincial social welfare and development officer, a provincial general services officer, a provincial agriculturist, and a provincial veterinarian. 4 Section 387. Chief Officials and Offices - xxx (b) There shall also be in every barangay a lupong tagapamayapa. The sangguniang barangay may form community brigades and create such other positions or offices as may be deemed necessary to

Moreover, Section 396 of the LGC states that "(T)he qualifications, duties, and functions of all other barangay officials appointed by the punong barangay shall be governed by the provisions of this Code and other laws or by barangay ordinances." Further, Sec. 76 of the LGC provides that "(E)very local government unit shall design and implement its own organizational structure and staffing pattern taking into consideration its service requirements and financial capability, subject to the minimum standards and guidelines prescribed by the Civil Service Commission." In other words, the Sangguniang Barangay may create positions such as that of a Barangay Administrator. However, this is subject to budgetary limitations on personal services and existing Civil Service Commission guidelines. As regards the Municipal Budget Office's directive to remove a Barangay Administrator on the ground that only persons with a law degree or graduate of courses related to public administration may hold the position, we surmise that this may have been based on Sec. 480 of the LGC which requires the Administrator to be a "holder of a college degree, preferably in public administration, law or any related course". However, this specifically applies to Administrators in the provincial, city and municipal levels. Based on the foregoing, the qualifications of a Barangay Administrator shall be based not on Sec. 480 of the LGC but on the barangay ordinance creating the position and prescribing qualifications for the same. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concem accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs carry out the purposes of the barangay government in accordance with the needs of public service, subject to tie budgetary limitations on personal services prescribed under Title Five, Book II of this Code.
